code: hb_blob_create ((const char *)data, size, HB_MEMORY_MODE_READONLY, NULL, NULL);
note: The fuzzer treats the entire attacker-controlled byte stream as a font blob.
The blob is parsed as a font face, so malformed input can influence all later table lookups and subset serialization.
The face is queried for cmap data before subsetting, exercising parser state derived from the input.
A subset plan is created and later drives serialization of selected tables.
The subset request selects a fixed set of Unicode codepoints, forcing the subsetter to build cmap and related tables from the attacker-controlled face.
The subset plan captures source-face metadata and the requested glyph/unicode retention policy.
The subsetter enumerates tables from the attacker-controlled font and decides which ones to serialize.
Each kept table is serialized into the destination buffer using hb_serialize_context_t.
During packing, the serializer looks up the current object in a hashmap keyed by object_t pointers.
The object is inserted into the hashmap after being moved into packed storage; the MSAN report points to this hashmap path as the use-of-uninitialized-value sink.
